title: Draft: BLF: Storing generated BLF-names in names not description

notes.body:
Given:
1. The fact that `if_name` always represented the human-readable BLF interface name,
2. `if_description` has been used in a release version of Wireshark and not just in master to store BLF channel numbers,
3. there are files out there converted from BLF to pcapng with the established meanings of this two fields,
4. users and/or automated filters could rely on them,
5. the fact that the two fields have very different meanings across platform anyway,

I would avoid swapping the two around. The benefits look negligible and #21069 can be solved by improving the dialog.

I guess "terminology wise" the current way, with putting the channel/HW IDs in the description, also makes more sense.

The AppText entries for channels does mainly use the attribute name "network" to denote the name for a channel (so no direct/immediate guidance to either Name or Description there) but for the Ethernet channels the <eli> elements for the ports part of a channel uses "name=" as part of the element text. Form my quick understanding the port name is combined with the channel network to build the complete name.

So, the only mention in the XML metadata of "native" BLF files seems to use the term name, at least for the individual Ethernet ports, while it does not seem to use the term description at all.
